text:
maria_support: Heads-up: ACME ticket — customer reports streaming sessions dropping with 'broken pipe' and those closes are being counted as 5xx in billing. They attached a curl trace and a short repro. Anyone seen this pattern?

maria_support: ```
$ curl -v -N -H "Authorization: Bearer ..." -X POST https://gateway.redwood.ai/v1/stream \n  -d '{"model":"redwood-small-v1","prompt":"hello"}'
* Connected to gateway.redwood.ai (1.2.3.4) port 443 (#0)
> POST /v1/stream HTTP/1.1
> Host: gateway.redwood.ai
> Transfer-Encoding: chunked
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
< Content-Type: text/event-stream
* Connection #0 to host gateway.redwood.ai left intact
* curl: (56) Recv failure: Connection was reset
```

jake_sre: Can you paste the request id / any proxy log IDs? Also what account and customer id?

maria_support: req_id: req_0a1b2c, account: 4321, customer: acme-inc. Proxy snippet shows: 
```
2025-03-10T12:04:12Z proxy[gw-01] INFO req=req_0a1b2c route=streaming upstream=10.10.8.23 status=200 bytes=2048
2025-03-10T12:04:24Z proxy[gw-01] WARN req=req_0a1b2c upstream=10.10.8.23 event=upstream_connection_reset 
```

nina_runtime: Looks like gateway is sending a FIN while the client is still reading. Which client stack is this? http/1.1 chunked or http/2? Also which runtime version & model?

maria_support: Client is HTTP/1.1 chunked (VS Code extension -> node-fetch). Model redwood-small-v1, runtime build 2025.02.12. Customer attached a tcpdump link — shows RST originating from upstream after ~12s of idle during streaming. They say we billed tokens up to EOF and are contesting billing.

oliver_billing: Please put a temporary billing hold for account 4321 until we confirm. Tagging billing ops.

jake_sre: I'll try to repro locally. Quick check: are we seeing half-close detection (FIN -> treat as client abort) or an actual RST from backend? If it's FIN from gateway we can change classification to client-abort. If it's RST from upstream that's different.

maria_support: Repro steps customer provided: (1) open session, (2) send ~700-token prompt, (3) server streams tokens for ~6-12s, (4) client sees ECONNRESET/"broken pipe" and stops. Customer reports we still counted tokens to EOF.

nina_runtime: Hypothesis: proxy idle-timeout or keepalive miscoordination with upstream model process. Two mitigations: increase proxy keepalive/idle timeout (10s -> 30s) and add heuristic to prefer FIN (graceful close) detection over RST when classifying billing. I'll push a canary for the keepalive tweak. :thinking_face:

deploybot: Canary deploy 2025-03-10-keepalive-tweak -> 10% rolled out

jake_sre: If we can't change timeouts immediately, we should change the metering heuristic: treat client-side connection close that occurs after a burst of streamed chunks as client abort (no 5xx). I'll open an ops ticket and a PR for the classifier. :+1:

oliver_billing: Billing hold created for account 4321 (ticket BILL-6712). We'll wait for final classification before issuing any credits.

maria_support: Customer asked for a minimal repro they can run locally. Pasting an example Node snippet they used: 
```
// node repro: triggers client abort after 7s
const http = require('http');
const req = http.request({
  host: 'gateway.redwood.ai',
  path: '/v1/stream',
  method: 'POST',
  headers: {'Authorization': 'Bearer ...', 'Transfer-Encoding': 'chunked'}
}, res => {
  res.on('data', d => process.stdout.write(d));
  res.on('end', () => console.log('stream end'))
});
req.write(JSON.stringify({model:'redwood-small-v1', prompt: 'longstream'}));
setTimeout(() => req.destroy(), 7000); // simulate client abort
```

nina_runtime: Perfect, thanks. I'll run that against the canary and capture /proc/net/tcp + kernel timestamps to see FIN vs RST timing. Tagging @jake_sre.

maria_support: I'll keep the customer updated and attach any additional tcpdumps they send.

jake_sre: I'll follow up with the PR and link logs here.

oliver_billing: Thanks everyone, keep the thread updated so we can finalize billing decision.
